newsitem.title: FRANCE: Sommer head sees higher '96 sales, profit.
newsitem.headline: Sommer head sees higher '96 sales, profit.

text.p: The chairman of French car parts maker Sommer-Allibert expects 1996 turnover to rise around nine percent, with a similar increase in profit.
"Profits should have increased by the same amount," Marc Assa said in an interview with weekly Journal des Finances, made available to Reuters on Friday.
The company's dividend policy will be maintained, he said. In previous years, dividend payments represented 30-40 percent of profits.
"This policy will be maintained," he said.
The company said last October when it reported first-half earnings that it expected higher 1996 profits, thanks to increased sales and stable raw material prices.
On a like-for-like basis, 1996 turnover rose four percent to 13.8 billion francs and should be above 15 billion in 1997 and should exceed 20 billion in 2000.
The auto sector will contribute nearly 10 billion francs in sales in 1997, up from 7.7 billion. The stock closed at 160 francs, down from 166.70 on Thursday.
